Saint Seraphim of Sarov

Icons

Saints

Saint Seraphim of Sarov

St. Seraphim of Sarov · Seraphim the Wonderworker

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Galatians 5:22–23

1 Thessalonians 5:16–18

Matthew 5:14–16

King James Version · Scripture previews

The OCA’s life identifies Seraphim as the Russian ascetic born Prochorus Moshnin in Kursk. It recounts his monastic life at Sarov, periods of solitude and prayer, and later ministry receiving people who sought counsel and consolation.

[1] Opening paragraphs; account of Sarov and later eldership

What is depicted

The selected icon is dated after 1903 and tentatively associated with the Seraphimo-Diveevsky Monastery workshop. It presents the elderly, white-bearded Seraphim holding a cross. This portrait differs from narrative icons showing him praying upon a rock or with visitors.

[2] File description and displayed historic reproduction

History and tradition

The OCA’s feast account dates his glorification to 1903, seventy years after his repose, and describes the translation and public veneration of his relics during the celebrations. The account distinguishes memorial services before the glorification from the festivities that followed.

[3] Opening paragraph; account of the July 1903 festivities

Published explanation

In a published sermon, Metropolitan Hilarion relates Seraphim’s long prayer in the forest and on a rock to the loving kindness that drew people to him. The account presents his example within the Church’s received memory, rather than prescribing his ascetic labors to beginners.

[4] Sermon paragraphs on the forest, rock, and visitors

But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.

[5] Galatians 5:22–23
